# EEG datasets


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

This page catalogs open EEG data: the places it is published, and the
datasets themselves with their rough size. It is a map for finding data,
not a benchmark. Every number comes from the dataset’s own page or
paper, and a blank means the source doesn’t report it.

Benchmark libraries cover one paradigm family each: 200 of MOABB’s 206
datasets, for example, are BCI paradigms (motor imagery, ERP, SSVEP and
c-VEP), and it loads none of the large clinical or sleep corpora. Labs
also tend to publish to one repository each, so no single source sees
everything. The tables below span EEG repositories, general-purpose
repositories, clinical corpora and lab websites.

The catalog is two CSV files in the repo,
[`catalog/sources.csv`](https://github.com/bkowshik/temple-of-eeg-decoding/blob/main/catalog/sources.csv)
and
[`catalog/datasets.csv`](https://github.com/bkowshik/temple-of-eeg-decoding/blob/main/catalog/datasets.csv),
so you can load, filter or correct it. Each row there also records the
license, the reference, the page its numbers came from, and notes on how
they were counted, including which numbers are approximate. Numbers were
gathered on 3 November 2026.

**Access:**

- **open**: download directly, no account
- **registration**: free account or login
- **DUA**: signed data use agreement or credentialed access
- **request**: apply to the lab or authors

**Trials** counts trials across all subjects and sessions; **hours** is
total recording time. Dataset tables are sorted by number of subjects,
and each name links to the dataset’s landing page.

The split holds even inside one benchmark. MOABB’s own table of its 206
datasets puts 54 on Zenodo, 19 of them from French labs such as
GIPSA-lab and Inria. It puts 21 on PhysioNet, 20 of which are studies
from a single P300 collection, bigP3BCI. All 19 on BNCI Horizon 2020
come from European labs, 8 of them Austrian. Figshare holds 17, OSF 13,
and Harvard Dataverse 10, 7 of them from Chinese labs. All 4 on GigaDB
come from Korean labs. Only 3 are on OpenNeuro, and 31 name no
repository at all.

## Where EEG data lives

Three kinds of places publish EEG data. Counts are as each source
reported them on 3 November 2026.

### General-purpose repositories

Repositories that hold any kind of data and don’t tag EEG reliably. The
count is search hits for “EEG”, which overstates how many EEG datasets
they hold: Zenodo’s hits even include Germany’s renewable-energy law,
which is also abbreviated EEG. Much lab-published BCI data lives here
all the same.

<td><a href="https://huggingface.co/datasets?search=eeg">Hugging Face
Hub</a></td>
<td style="text-align: right;">1,001</td>
<td>mixed</td>
<td>datasets whose name matches ‘eeg’, of which 738 are EEGDash mirrors
of NEMAR/OpenNeuro data; a further 13 datasets sit under the braindecode
org. The remaining ~260 are user uploads of mixed provenance and
licence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><a href="https://dataverse.harvard.edu">Harvard Dataverse</a></td>
<td style="text-align: right;">535</td>
<td>mixed</td>
<td>datasets returned by the Search API for q=EEG, type=dataset. 10
MOABB BCI datasets live here, 7 from Chinese groups (Tianjin University,
CAS, World Robot Contest) and 2 from Japan.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><a href="https://data.mendeley.com">Mendeley Data</a></td>
<td style="text-align: right;">413</td>
<td>open</td>
<td>results attributed to Mendeley Data for query=EEG on its search page
(419 across all indexed sources). Elsevier’s repository; its 5 MOABB
datasets come from Mexico, Ecuador, Indonesia and Turkey.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><a href="https://nda.nih.gov">NIMH Data Archive (NDA)</a></td>
<td style="text-align: right;">278</td>
<td>DUA</td>
<td>collections matching ‘EEG’ in NDA’s search API (80 match
‘electroencephalography’). EEG from NIH-funded mental-health studies
(autism, psychosis, depression, adolescent sleep); access needs an
institutionally signed Data Use Certification.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><a href="https://ieee-dataport.org">IEEE DataPort</a></td>
<td style="text-align: right;">213</td>
<td>mixed</td>
<td>results for site search ‘EEG’: 181 standard datasets (subscription),
24 open access, 8 competitions. Mostly single-lab engineering datasets,
often from consumer headsets (e.g., the Emotiv-based STEW workload
set).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><a href="https://datadryad.org">Dryad</a></td>
<td style="text-align: right;">157</td>
<td>open</td>
<td>hits for q=EEG in the Dryad search API (60 for
‘electroencephalography’). Journal-linked CC0 deposits, human and
animal; few large curated EEG collections.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><a href="https://gin.g-node.org">G-Node GIN</a></td>
<td style="text-align: right;">45</td>
<td>open</td>
<td>public repositories matching ‘EEG’ from the GIN API, including forks
and DOI copies. Small German/Swiss footprint (MPIB Berlin, USZ Zurich
scalp EEG + iEEG, mouse hdEEG).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><a href="https://search.kg.ebrains.eu">EBRAINS Knowledge
Graph</a></td>
<td style="text-align: right;">42</td>
<td>mixed</td>
<td>datasets matching ‘EEG’ (21 tagged electroencephalography; 13
controlled access, 12 free, 9 embargoed, 8 restricted). European Human
Brain Project labs, e.g., TMS-EEG perturbational complexity and
sEEG/hd-EEG stimulation studies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><a href="https://www.synapse.org">Synapse (Sage
Bionetworks)</a></td>
<td style="text-align: right;">25</td>
<td>mixed</td>
<td>public projects matching ‘EEG’ in the Synapse search API, several
unrelated (e.g., mPower). Hosts TD-BRAIN (Brainclinics), BrainLat,
HarMNqEEG multinational cross-spectra and FACED; access terms vary by
project.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><a href="https://dandiarchive.org">DANDI Archive</a></td>
<td style="text-align: right;">23</td>
<td>open</td>
<td>dandisets matching ‘EEG’; mostly animal and intracranial (iEEG/sEEG,
single-unit) recordings. DANDI is the BRAIN Initiative’s NWB archive,
with little human scalp EEG.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><a href="https://gigadb.org">GigaDB</a></td>
<td style="text-align: right;">8</td>
<td>open</td>
<td>8 EEG datasets among the 11 hits for ‘EEG’ in the GigaDB search API.
Data notes for GigaScience; all 4 MOABB datasets here are Korean (Korea
University OpenBMI Lee2019, GIST Cho2017).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><a href="https://archive.ics.uci.edu">UCI Machine Learning
Repository</a></td>
<td style="text-align: right;">4</td>
<td>open</td>
<td>4 datasets match ‘EEG’ in its API (EEG Database, EEG Eye State, EEG
SSVEP signals, BEED epilepsy). Small, old ML-benchmark staples.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

faces, EEGBCI, mTRF, Kiloword, Sleep PSG, ERP CORE, SSVEP, EyeLink
EEG-eyetracking); LIMO is also EEG but not labelled so. Most other
fetchers are MEG, OPM, sEEG/ECoG or phantoms; teaching-sized, not
benchmarks.</td>
</tr>
